arxiv-2102-12295.title: Image Augmentation for Multitask Few-Shot Learning: Agricultural Domain Use-Case
arxiv-2102-12295.creator: Sergey Nesteruk, Dmitrii Shadrin, Mariia Pukalchik
arxiv-2102-12295.description: Abstract Large datasets’ availability is catalyzing a rapid expansion of deep learning in general and computer vision in particular. At the same time, in many domains, a sufficient amount of training data is lacking, which may become an obstacle to the practical application of computer vision techniques.

arxiv-2112-11352.title: Unsupervised quark/gluon jet tagging with Poissonian Mixture Models Preprint: IPPP/21/58 & ICAS 70/21
arxiv-2112-11352.creator: E. Alvarez, M. Spannowsky, and M. Szewc
arxiv-2112-11352.description: Abstract The classification of jets induced by quarks or gluons is important for New Physics searches at high-energy colliders. However, available taggers usually rely on modelling the data through Monte Carlo simulations, which could veil intractable theoretical and systematical uncertainties.

arxiv-2211-03368.title: Anisotropic gravitational waves induced by hypermagnetic fields during the electroweak phase transition epoch
arxiv-2211-03368.creator: Mingqiu Li, Qi-Shu Yan, Mei Huang
arxiv-2211-03368.description: Abstract We study the anisotropies of gravitational waves induced by weak hypermagnetic fields which are randomly distributed and oriented during the electroweak phase transition in the early universe. The theory setup of this study is the standard model plus a real singlet scalar field, which can produce the needed strongly first order electroweak phase transition.

arxiv-2304-01365.title: Finding a Burst of Positives via Nonadaptive Semiquantitative Group Testing
arxiv-2304-01365.creator: Yun-Han Li a , Ryan Gabrys b , Jin Sima a , Ilan Shomorony a and Olgica Milenkovic a
arxiv-2304-01365.description: Abstract Motivated by testing for pathogenic diseases we consider a new nonadaptive group testing problem for which: (1) positives occur within a burst, capturing the fact that infected test subjects often come in clusters, and (2) that the test outcomes arise from semiquantitative measurements that provide coarse information about the number of positives in any tested group.

arxiv-2402-18159.title: Provable Risk-Sensitive Distributional Reinforcement Learning with General Function Approximation
arxiv-2402-18159.creator: Yu Chen, Xiangcheng Zhang, Siwei Wang, Longbo Huang
arxiv-2402-18159.description: Abstract In the realm of reinforcement learning (RL), accounting for risk is crucial for making decisions under uncertainty, particularly in applications where safety and reliability are paramount. In this paper, we introduce a general framework on Risk-Sensitive Distributional Reinforcement Learning (RS-DisRL), with static Lipschitz Risk Measures (LRM) and general function approximation.

arxiv-2410-04586.title: Rational Normal Curves in Weighted Projective Space
arxiv-2410-04586.creator: Caitlin M. Davis, Aleksandra Sobieska
arxiv-2410-04586.description: Abstract . This article aims to extend classical homological results about the rational normal curves to analogues in weighted projective spaces. Results include determinantality and nonstandard versions of quadratic generation and the Koszul property. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 13D02 1. Introduction This article aims to extend classical homological results about the rational normal curves to their weighted analogues.

arxiv-2507-05517.title: Empowering Healthcare Practitioners with Language Models: Structuring Speech Transcripts in Two Real-World Clinical Applications
arxiv-2507-05517.creator: Jean-Philippe Corbeil, Asma Ben Abacha, George Michalopoulos
arxiv-2507-05517.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4o and o1 have demonstrated strong performance on clinical natural language processing (NLP) tasks across multiple medical benchmarks. Nonetheless, two high-impact NLP tasks — structured tabular reporting from nurse dictations and medical order extraction from doctor-patient consultations — remain underexplored due to data scarcity and sensitivity, despite active industry efforts.

pmc-10494917.title: Exploring the Relationship Between Stress and Satisfaction During Clinical Training Among Respiratory Therapy Students: A Nationwide Cross-Sectional Survey
pmc-10494917.creator: Rayan Siraj, Abdulelah M Aldhahir, Jaber S Alqahtani, Samah Bakhadlq, Saeed Alghamdi, Abdullah A Alqarni, Turki M Alanazi, Abdullah Alruwaili, Saleh S Algarni, Abdulrhman S Alghamd, Mushabbab Alahmari, Abdulmajeed Baogbah, Nawaf A Alsolami, Mufleh Alrougi, Kamal Hamed Al Khodidi, Fahad Alahmadi

There is limited information on stress and satisfaction perceived by clinical-level undergraduate students studying respiratory therapy (RT) in Saudi Arabia.MethodsA descriptive, cross-sectional study design with an online questionnaire was employed to conduct this study.

pmc-11358885.title: Constructing Multifunctional Composite Single Crystals via Polymer Gel Incorporation
pmc-11358885.creator: Zhiwen Mao, Jie Ren, Hanying Li
pmc-11358885.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The non-uniformity of a single crystal can sometimes be found in biominerals, where surrounding biomacromolecules are incorporated into the growing crystals. This unique composite structure, combining heterogeneity and long-range ordering, enables the functionalization of single crystals. Polymer gel media are often used to prepare composite single crystals, in which the growing crystals incorporate gel networks and form a bi-continuous interpenetrating structure without any disruption to single crystallinity.

pmc-12398907.title: Rapid beta-blocker up-titration enhances cardiac adrenergic innervation improvement in dilated cardiomyopathy
pmc-12398907.creator: Ewa Dziewięcka, Katarzyna Holcman, Magdalena Kostkiewicz, Wojciech Szot, Sylwia Wiśniowska-Śmiałek, Mateusz Winiarczyk, Natalia Przytuła, Agnieszka Stępień-Wroniecka, Katarzyna Graczyk, Małgorzata Mazur, Agata Leśniak-Sobelga, Jarosław Gąsiorek, Agnieszka Czapska, Jan Jamroś, Karolina Garlicka, Pawe
pmc-12398907.description: Graphical abstract In heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), chronic hyperactivation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) and the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) leads to adverse cardiac remodeling and symptom progression [1,2]. A multi-level neurohormonal blockade with RAAS inhibitors and β-blockers (BB) is both safe and prognostically beneficial, regardless of HF etiology [ischemic vs. non-ischemic, including dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM)] [3].

pmc-12422068.title: Clinical Course of Iris Retraction Syndrome Associated With Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment: A Report of Three Cases
pmc-12422068.creator: Keigo Takagi, Kazunobu Sugihara, Mizuki Iida, Kana Murakami, Chisako Ida, Hinako Ohtani, Masaki Tanito
pmc-12422068.description: This report describes three cases of iris retraction syndrome (IRS) associated with long-standing rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD), all presenting with hypotony, abnormally deep anterior chambers, and ciliary body detachment, often accompanied by dense cataracts and uveitis-like findings that initially obscured the underlying pathology.

pmc-12605942.title: Plasma proteins and osteosarcoma risk: causal evidence from Mendelian randomization
pmc-12605942.creator: Hanjun Ma, Ju Liao, Zonglong He, Mingxuan Liu, Fengxu Wei, Qi Wei, Qunqiang Luo
pmc-12605942.description: Osteosarcoma (OS) is an exceptionally aggressive bone cancer, and the identification of blood-based biomarkers for early detection and prognosis remains a significant challenge. This study aimed to investigate the causal relationships between circulating plasma proteins and OS risk using Mendelian randomization (MR).

pmc-12612263.title: The consumption of onion extract tablet modulates expression of human plasma microRNAs: a randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial
pmc-12612263.creator: Mao Yamamoto, Yoshinori Fujimura, Ryotaro Chiba, Modena Shimizu, Motofumi Kumazoe, Akane Haseda, Jun Nishihira, Mari Maeda-Yamamoto, Hirofumi Tachibana
pmc-12612263.description: MicroRNAs (miRNAs), which are non-coding RNAs of approximately 20 nucleotides in length, have attracted attention for their involvement in various biological processes and the regulation of diseases. However, the effects of foods and supplements on miRNA expression in vivo remain unclear.

pmc-12617109.title: OA2035. Rockfall hazards in Austria’s hiking network: A GIS-based spatial risk assessment
pmc-12617109.creator: T Fian, A Kaltenegger, T Lücksmann, C Trauner-Karner
pmc-12617109.description: Issue/ProblemAustria’s hiking network is increasingly affected by rockfall hazards, especially in areas with unstable geological conditions. These hazards pose a significant risk to hikers, contributing to injuries and fatalities. The ongoing effects of climate change, such as the thawing of permafrost, potentially increase the risk, making it more critical to assess and address rockfall dangers.

pmc-12630692.title: Optimizing wireless sensor networks using fuzzy triangular snake graph models and fuzzy topological indices
pmc-12630692.creator: Atef F. Hashem, Shama Liaqat, Zeeshan Saleem Mufti, Muhammad Farhan Hanif

Its practical applications in wireless sensor network (WSN) is also designed.

pmc-12638223.title: Vomiting Blood, Missing the Heart: A Rare Presentation of Acute Myocardial Infarction
pmc-12638223.creator: Suad Albulushi, Nina Farazan, Yasmeen AlHarmali, Ahmadreza Bagheri
pmc-12638223.description: Hematemesis, the vomiting of blood, is an uncommon initial manifestation of myocardial infarction (MI). We describe a case involving the clinical progression of a 46-year-old man who arrived at the emergency department with symptoms including active coffee ground vomitus and severe epigastric pain.

pmc-12729554.title: The Role of Lower Limb Kinetics in Boxing Punches and the Impact of Fatigue on Biomechanical Performance
pmc-12729554.creator: Charles Stewart, Ross Cornett, Julien S Baker, Yaodong Gu, Frédéric Dutheil, Ukadike Chris Ugbolue, Philippe Gorce
pmc-12729554.description: Purpose: This study investigated the contribution of lower limb kinetics to punch performance in amateur boxing and examined the effects of fatigue on biomechanical efficiency. Methods: Ten male amateur boxers performed six punch types (jab, cross, left hook, right hook, left uppercut, right uppercut) under non-fatigued and post-fatigue conditions.

pmc-13033513.title: The Medical Student Performance Evaluation in global medical education: addressing a missing Middle Eastern perspective
pmc-13033513.creator: Abdullah Jabri, Bader Taftafa, Mohamed Alsharif, Abdulaziz Mhannayeh, Dania Sibai, Abderrahman Ouban, Fouad F. Jabri
pmc-13033513.description: BackgroundAn essential part of the residency selection process is the Medical Student Performance Evaluation (MSPE), which provides an organized overview of the performance of undergraduate medical students. Despite the Association of American Medical Colleges’ (AAMC) extensive guidelines, there is still considerable variation in MSPE content, interpretation, and application among schools.

pmc-13331110.title: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13331110.creator: James French, Lucy Bomphrey, Aspasia Manta, Katie Scandrett, Kashish Malhotra, Punith Kempegowda
pmc-13331110.description: Current knowledge of hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state (HHS) is drawn from case series and small observational cohorts, limiting applicability to broader clinical practice. There is a lack of robust, large-scale studies exploring triggers of HHS and associated mortality. This absence of reliable data impedes prevention strategies, tailored clinical guidelines, and equitable resource allocation.

pmc-13368642.title: Warm sitz bath as an adjunctive therapy for distal ureteral calculi ≤5 mm: a prospective study
pmc-13368642.creator: Li-diao Li, Jing-jing Lou, Ze-peng Wu, Xiang Hu, Hai-ou Lv, Yu-han He
pmc-13368642.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the efficacy of warm sitz bath (WSB) as an adjunctive conservative therapy for patients with distal ureteral calculi (DUC) ≤5 mm.MethodsA total of 131 eligible patients with DUC ≤5 mm were prospectively randomized into the WSB group or the control group.
